name: Hypoplastic Amelogenesis Imperfecta

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiographic Diagnostic Criteria for Amelogenesis Imperfecta

criteria.description: Markedly reduced enamel thickness visible clinically and radiographically
Enamel is hard but thin, leading to rough or pitted tooth surfaces
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant or recessive inheritance
Radiographs show normal dentin thickness with thin radiopaque enamel layer
No systemic or metabolic abnormalities explaining enamel defects

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of markedly reduced enamel thickness clinically and radiographically with characteristic enamel hardness and radiographic appearance; family history supportive but not mandatory.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may confirm mutations in genes such as AMELX, ENAM, or MMP20.

pathognomonic.notes: Enamel thickness significantly reduced across all teeth

pathognomonic.symptomName: Pitted and rough enamel surface texture
pathognomonic.notes: Surface irregularities due to defective enamel formation
searchTerms: tooth surface with pits and grooves

pathognomonic.symptomName: Normal dentin thickness with enamel hypoplasia
pathognomonic.notes: Radiographic hallmark distinguishing from dentin defects
searchTerms: enamel growth defect with intact dentin

common.symptomName: Increased tooth sensitivity to thermal stimuli
common.notes: Due to thin enamel exposing dentin
searchTerms: teeth sensitive to hot and cold

common.symptomName: Yellow to brown discoloration of teeth
searchTerms: teeth with dark yellow or brown color

common.notes: Fragile enamel prone to mechanical damage

searchTerms: late coming in of adult teeth

occasional.symptomName: Malocclusion due to abnormal tooth morphology
occasional.notes: Altered occlusal relationships secondary to enamel defects
searchTerms: bad bite due to tooth shape

occasional.notes: Due to enamel defects and plaque retention

searchTerms: teeth hurt when eating acid foods

rare.notes: Rare morphological anomaly of tooth roots
searchTerms: thin enamel with large tooth pulp chambers
enamel underdevelopment with enlarged tooth roots
enamel defect combined with taurodont teeth

rare.notes: Rare cases with combined enamel and dentin abnormalities

laboratory: Normal serum calcium and phosphate levels
imaging: Panoramic radiographs showing thin radiopaque enamel layer with normal dentin
No evidence of dentin or pulp abnormalities
genetic: Mutations in ENAM gene (autosomal dominant/recessive forms)
other: Family history consistent with hereditary enamel defects
Clinical examination revealing characteristic enamel hypoplasia

distinguishingFeatures: Normal enamel thickness but soft and mottled enamel
Enamel chips easily due to poor mineralization
Diffuse white to brown enamel discoloration

redFlags: Rapid enamel loss leading to severe tooth sensitivity
Early onset of dental caries despite good oral hygiene
Family history of similar enamel defects indicating hereditary pattern
